title: Fortalitium Fidei
shelf_note: Alfonso de Espina's Latin treatise against heretics, Jews and Saracens, printed in 1487 in two-column gothic type. It belongs on a medieval-literature (arlima) shelf and in the patron library.
structure_note: The structure count gives pages_translated 0, but the book field gives 504 and this page has a translation. That is an instrument mismatch (E2), not missing translations. Only 26 of 506 pages have a printed number. The leaf shows a running head ('Liber' / 'Secundus') and no folio, so the 10 backsteps and 13 repeats most likely come from reading running heads or stray numerals as page numbers, not from a scan splice.

missing.english: Such a person sins "under God," because he grieves that he is in sin.
missing.why: the contrast between sinning 'under God' and 'against God' (sub deo / in deum) is a scholastic distinction the argument depends on, and the English does not explain it

missing.english: what he prays in the person of the Church, when he says "Let us pray,"
missing.why: 'in the person of the Church' (in persona ecclesiae) is a technical sacramental notion: the priest prays as the Church's minister, so the prayer's effect does not depend on his merit. The English does not explain it

missing.english: as much of the purgatorial penalty as the bishop relaxed in this present world
missing.why: 'relaxed' / 'relaxation' is the technical language of indulgences (remission of temporal penalty), and a general reader will not recognise it

book_verdict: The right leaf, with a faithful and readable translation. A few OCR misreadings of abbreviations ('Dicimus' to 'Diceret', 'Sciendum' to 'Secundum', 'vestra' to 'vita') carry over as small shifts in sense. One translator's note wrongly blames the printed text for an OCR misread. Nothing here is serious.
